newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells 63 percent of KABO.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells 63 percent of KABO.

text.p: The Egyptian state sold 63 percent of Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles for 196.86 million pounds ($57.99 million) on Wednesday in the biggest privatisation operation for about 10 weeks.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said the state sold 1,930,000 Kabo shares at 102.00 pounds a share, the minimum bid price in the auction. Reuters had erroneously reported that the minimum bid price was 109.00 pounds.
Brokers said the bids ranged from 102.00 to about 108.00, with most of them in the lower part of the range.
They also said that the state-owned National Bank of Egypt stepped in at the last minute to bring the number of shares sold up to the government's target of 1.93 million shares.

The sale puts Kabo firmly in the private sector but the state's Holding Company for Spinning and Weaving retains a small stake. The state had already sold the private sector 29.95 percent of the 3,062,000 shares in the company.
Kabo makes clothes under its own label and for international brands like JIL, Jockey, British Home Stores and Wrangler.

Stock exchange figures showed Kabo made after-tax profits of 6.872 million pounds in the third quarter of the financial year 1996/7, against 2.868 million in the same period of 1995/6. The years start July 1.
